overview: This Senate resolution marks the tenth anniversary of the June 17, 2015, shooting at Mother Emanuel African Methodist Episcopal (AME) Church in Charleston, South Carolina, where a white supremacist gunman killed nine Black parishioners during a Bible study and prayer meeting. It describes the life of each of the nine victims, known as the Emanuel Nine, and notes that the killer was convicted of federal hate crimes and sentenced to death, and also pleaded guilty to state murder charges. The resolution honors the victims' memory, cites the congregation's faith and forgiveness in the aftermath, and also recognizes the survivors. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on June 17, 2025.
for: Supporters say naming and remembering each victim honors their lives and recognizes the congregation's response to a racially motivated attack.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and doesn't change any law or spending.
